chapter_title_ka: ამბავი ავთანდილისა, ასმათს რომ ეუბნების ქვაბშიგან
chapter_title_en: Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave
chapter_expert_explanation_en: At the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ჩამოვიდა, ცხენი ახსნა, მისგან ხესა გამობმული,
ზედა შეჯდა, გაემართა, ქვაბი დახვდა კარ-განხმული;
მუნით ქალი გამოიჭრა გულ-მდუღარე, ცრემლ-დასხმული,
და ეგონა თუ, დაბრუნდაო პირი ვარდი, ბროლ-ბაკმული.
stanzas.english_translation: She knew not the face, it was not like the face of that knight; swiftly she turned, with a cry she made for rock and tree; the knight leaped from his horse, seized her like a partridge in a net; the rocks resounded with the maid's monotonous cry.

stanzas.english_translation: She yielded not to that knight; even the sight of him was hateful. Like a partridge under an eagle she fluttered hither and thither; she called on a certain Tariel for help, but he succoured her not. Avt’handil threw himself on his knees; he entreated her with his fingers.

მას ყმასა თავი არ მისცა, ჭვრეტადცა ებილწებოდა,
ვითა კაკაბი არწივსა ქვეშე, მიდამო ძრწებოდა,

stanzas.english_translation: He said: "Hush! what (ill) can I do thee? I am a man of Adam's race. I have seen those roses and violets grown pale. Tell me something of him. Who is the cypress-formed, the halo-faced? I shall do nought else to thee, be comforted, cry not thus loudly."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 232; Wardrop Stanza 229): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: The weeping girl, like a suppliant for justice, said: "If thou be not mad, let me go; if thou art mad, return to reason. Now thou lightly askest me to tell thee a very hard matter; try not in vain, look not to me to tell his story."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 233; Wardrop Stanza 230): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: Again she said: "O knight, what wilt thou, or what dost thou request of me? This thing cannot be even written with the pen. Once thou shalt say 'Tell me!' a hundred times I shall tell thee 'No!' As smiling is better than weeping, so I prefer mourning to song."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 234; Wardrop Stanza 231): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: "Maiden, thou knowest not whence I come, what woes I have endured! For as long as I have sought tidings, from none have I heard them. I have found thee; however much my words may annoy thee, I cannot let thee go till thou tell me. Be not bashful with me."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 235; Wardrop Stanza 232): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: The maiden said: "Why have I fallen in with thee? Who am I? or who art thou? The sun is not near me, this thou knewest, O hoarfrost, therefore thou thus annoyest me; long discourse is tedious, so I shall speak shortly to thee; on no account shall I tell thee aught, do whatsoever thou wilt."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 236; Wardrop Stanza 233): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. ქალმან უთხრა: “რას შეგესწარ, მე ვინ ვარ და ანუ შენო?
მზე არ მახლავს, შეგეტყვების, თრთვილო, ასრე მით მაწყენო;

stanzas.english_translation: Yet again he adjured her, he threw himself on his knees before her, but nought could he win from her; he wearied of entreaty, his indignation mounted to his face, blood flowed to his eyes, he arose, he drew her by the hair, he put a knife to her throat.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 237; Wardrop Stanza 234): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კვლაცა ჰკითხა ზენარობით, მიუყარნა მუხლნი წინა,
მაგრა ვერა ვერ დაჰყარა, მუდარობა მოეწყინა;
პირსა ზედა გაგულისდა, თვალთა სისხლი მოედინა,

stanzas.english_translation: Thus he spoke: "How can I forgive thee so much ill-will? If I weep, shall the tear be in vain? It is better for thee to tell me, I shall trouble thee no more; if not, may God slay mine enemy as I slay thee!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 238; Wardrop Stanza 235): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. რაგვარა თუ ამატირო, ცრემლი ცუდად დამადინო!

stanzas.english_translation: The maid replied: "Thou hast done exceeding ill to think of using force. If thou kill me not I shall not die; I am hale and alive. Why shall I tell thee anything until the time when I shall no longer see woes, and if thou kill me I shall have no head to converse with thee."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 239; Wardrop Stanza 236): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: Again she said: "Oh, why didst thou find me! who art thou that speakest with me? Who? I cannot be made to tell this story with living tongue. I will make thee kill me at mine own wish; like a despised letter, easily shalt thou tear me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 240; Wardrop Stanza 237): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. ეგე ამბავი ცოცხალსა ენითა ვერ მათქმევინო!
მე თავი ჩემი ნებითა ჩემითა მოგაკლვევინო,

stanzas.english_translation: "Think not that death would be suffering to me, for it would free me from weeping; it is the drier-up of the ford of tears; the whole world seems to me as straw, even so do I weigh it; I know not who thou art, that I should tell thee trusty words?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 241; Wardrop Stanza 238): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: The knight said (to himself): "Thus shall I not make her speak, I must think of some other way; it is better to ponder the matter." He let her go, and sat down apart; he wept, he began to shed tears. He said to the maiden: "I have angered thee; now I know not, alas! how I shall survive."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 242; Wardrop Stanza 239): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: The maiden sat morose, she is sulky, she is not yet sweetened. Avt’handil sits below weeping; no longer does he speak. In the rose-garden the pool of tears is dammed up. The maiden, too, weeps over yonder, her heart! softening towards him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 243; Wardrop Stanza 240): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: She pitied the weeping knight, therefore her hot tears flowed, but she sat, strange to the stranger, she spoke not. The knight perceived that her hasty thoughts towards him were calmed; with flowing tears he entreated her; he arose and bent his knee before her.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 244; Wardrop Stanza 241): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. ყმა მტირალი შეებრალა, ამად ცხელნი ცრემლნი ღვარნა,
მაგრა უჯდა უცხოს უცხო, არ ბაგენი აუბარნა;

და ცრემლ-დენილი შეეხვეწა, ადგა, მუხლნი მიუყარნა.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "I know that now I am by no means worthy to hope from thee; I have angered thee; I remain a stranger to thee and thus lonely; yet even now I have hope for myself from thee, for it is said that sin shall be forgiven unto seven times.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 245; Wardrop Stanza 242): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: "Though my beginning in service has pleased thee ill, it is fitting to pity the lover; understand thou this: from any other, whomsoever, I can have no aid, none is my strength. I yield thee my life for my heart's sake. What more can I do?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 246; Wardrop Stanza 243): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: When the maid heard from the knight of his love, with heart sobs she began to shed tears a hundredfold snore; again she raised her voice in wailing, she smiled not. God gave Avt’handil his wish, his heart's comfort.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 247; Wardrop Stanza 244): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.english_translation: He said (to himself): "These words have changed her colour; doubtless her tears flow faster (for that) she is mad for someone." He spoke once more: "O sister, a lover is pitied even by his foes; thou, too, knowest that he himself seeks death, he shuns it not.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 248; Wardrop Stanza 245): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
იტყვის თუ: “ამა სიტყვითა მას ფერი შეეცვალების,
ვისთვისმე ცხელი უცილოდ მას ცრემლი ემალმალების”.
კვლა უთხრა: “დაო, მიჯნური მტერთაცა შეებრალების,
და ესეცა იცი, სიკვდილსა თვით ეძებს, არ ეკრძალების.
stanzas.english_translation: "I am a lover, a madman to whom life is unbearable. My sun sent me to seek that knight. Even a cloud could not reach me where I have been on that quest. I have found thy heart; his to thee, thine to him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 249; Wardrop Stanza 246): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.english_translation: "His face I have imprinted on my heart like a (holy) picture. For him mad, cut off, have I given up all my joy. One of two things do thou to me: make me a prisoner or set me free, give me life or slay me, adding grief to grief."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 250; Wardrop Stanza 247): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მისი სახე გულსა ჩემსა ხატად ასრე გამოვხატე,
მისთვის ხელმან, გამოჭრილმან, ლხინი ჩემი ვაალქატე;
ორისაგან ერთი მიყავ: ტყვე მქმენ, ანუ მააზატე,
და ან მაცოცხლე, ანუ მომკალ, ჭირი ჭირსა მომიმატე”.
stanzas.english_translation: The maiden spoke to the knight a word more pleasant than her first: "What thou hast now thought of is much better; just now thou didst sow enmity in my heart, now thou hast found in me a friend more sisterly than a sister. 248a. "Then, since thou hast thought of love as thine aid, henceforth it will not be that I shall not be thy servant; if I devote not myself to thee, I shall make thee mad, I shall make thee sad; I shall die for thy sake if I find not some means to help thee.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 251; Wardrop Stanza 248): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

ერთი კაცი შემაქცევრად შენად ვითა დაგელია?
გეახლოს და არ გაშმაგდე, თუცა ჭირი არ გაკლია;
და შენ მოჰკვდე და იგი წახდეს, ესე შენთვის რა მადლია?”
stanzas.english_translation: The maid said: "Be not angry with me, I fear and entreat thee; since God has appointed me thy vizier, I cannot conceal the best that I know in the matter: to go to extremes is of no use; thou hast overstepped the bounds."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 273; Wardrop Stanza 270): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უბრძანა: “დაო, ეგეა მსგავსი შენისა გულისა,
მაგრა არ არის ქვეყანად წამალი ამა წყლულისა!
ვის ძალაქვს პოვნა კაცისა, თვით სოფლად არ მოსრულისა,
და ჩემი ლხინია სიკვდილი, გაყრა ხორცთა და სულისა.
stanzas.english_translation: The knight replied: "I know not what thou askest of me; tell me clearly. How can I create a man for my service without God? God needs me to be unhappy; what can I do? Of a truth I am become as a wild beast, to this pass have I brought myself."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 274; Wardrop Stanza 271): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ღმერთმან სხვაცა ეტლსა ჩემსა სადმცა კაცი რად დაბადა,
სიახლე და საუბარი თუმცა მისი მე მეწადა!
ვინმცა გასძლნა ჭირნი ჩემნი, ანუ ვინმცა შეეცადა?
და შენგან კიდე ხორციელი, დაო, მივის არასადა”.
stanzas.english_translation: The maid again spoke: "I have harassed thee with overmuch advice, but if I could find a man who would come to thee of his own freewill, who would stay near thee, who would rejoice thee by his acquaintance, wilt thou swear not to kill him nor do him any hurt?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 275; Wardrop Stanza 272): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქალმან ჰკადრა: “არ გამიწყრე, ვიშიშვი და ვიაჯ დია;
რათგან, ღმერთსა ვაზირობა შენი ჩემზედ მოუგდია,
ვერ დავმალავ უკეთესსა, რაცა საქმე გამიცდია.
და არა ვარგა უსაზომო, თავი ზომსა გარდგიხდია”.
stanzas.english_translation: He answered: "If thou wilt show him to me, greatly shall I rejoice at sight of him. (I swear) by the love of her for whose sake I wander mad in the fields, I shall do nought unpleasing, I shall never cause any bitterness to him; I shall be pleasant and love him, and do all I can to be amiable."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 276; Wardrop Stanza 273): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ყმამან უთხრა: “რას მენუკვი, არა ვიცი, გამიცხადე.
კაცი ჩემად სამსახურად უღმრთოდ მემცა ვით დავბადე!
ღმერთსა ჩემი უბედობა უნდა, მემცა რას ვეცადე!
და განაღამცა გავნადირდი, თავი ასრე გავიხადე”.
stanzas.english_translation: The maid rose and went to bring that knight. "He is not angry," quoth she, to encourage him. She took him by the hand and led him forth, like the full moon. When Tariel saw him he thought him like the sun.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 277; Wardrop Stanza 274): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქალმან კვლა ჰკადრა: “გაგსაჯე მეტითა შეგონებითა,
მაგრა თუ კაცი მოგგვარო, მოგყვეს თავისა ნებითა,
იგი გეახლოს, ილხენდე მისითა შემეცნებითა;
და ჰფიცე, არ მოჰკლა, არ იყო, არ-სავნებლისა ვნებითა”.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel met him. They were both fit to be ranked as suns, or as the moon in heaven, cloudless, spreading her rays on the plain beneath. Compared with them the aloe-tree was of no worth; they were like the seven planets; to what else shall I liken them?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 278; Wardrop Stanza 275): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. When she initially mistakes him for an enemy and refuses to speak, Avtandil overcomes her distrust by invoking the name of love ('mijnuroba'), persuading her to shelter him and introduce him to Tariel.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ყმამან უთხრა: “თუ მიჩვენებ, ვნახავ, დიდად გავიხარებ,
სიყვარულმან მისმან, ვისთვის ხელი მინდორს თავსა ვარებ,
არას ვუზამ უგემურსა, არა ოდეს გავამწარებ;
და რაცა ჩემგან ეამების, ვაამებ და შევიყვარებ”.
stanzas.english_translation: They kissed each other, they were not bashful at being strangers; they opened the rose, from their lips their white teeth shone transparent. They embraced each other's neck, together they wept; their jacinth, which was worth rubies, they turned into amber.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 8 ('Story of Avtandil Speaking with Asmat in the Cave', Stanza 279; Wardrop Stanza 276): Part of the narrative sequence in which at the cave hidden among rocks and reeds, Avtandil encounters the weeping maidservant Asmat. act_title: Act I: Arabia, The Royal Hunt & Quest for the Stranger Knight

location.desc: Tariel and Asmat's rocky refuge among the reed-beds, conquered from the Devis.

key_maxim_ka: მიჯნურობა არის ტურფა, საცოდნელად ძნელი გვარი
key_maxim_en: Chivalric love is fair, a kind hard to know.
